name: @graph-motor/sdk-js
description: Thin JS/TS wrapper over graph-wasm's raw extern "C" ABI: a lazy wasm loader, zero-copy typed-array column views, a typed-error Motor API, and the two source adapters for the role-based ingest contract. No wasm-bindgen. Ships no build, same as the repo root: run its .ts sources directly with Node's --experimental-strip-types, or bundle them yourself.
//devDependencies: No devDependencies of its own: it type-checks against the repo root's installed `typescript` (`npm ci` at the repo root), via `tsc -p crates/graph-sdk-js/tsconfig.json --noEmit`. Adding a second, separately-versioned `typescript` here would risk two compilers disagreeing about the same generated .d.ts.
//peerDependencies: The adapters are the only thing here that needs a runtime, and it is one already in every supported engine: `JSON.parse`/`JSON.stringify` and `TextEncoder`. There is no wasm loader dependency, no schema validator, and no `fetch` outside `./remote`, which calls the platform's own (or the one a caller passes) — the ingest contract's reader, its canonical writer and its JSON Schema all live in the Rust side, and `graph-cli ingest` runs them. A consumer that wants to validate a document in JavaScript before sending it should read `docs/contract/ingest-schema.json` with whatever validator they already have; adding one here would be a dependency this package does not otherwise need.
